key_insight: Mosaic extends agentic reinforcement learning to multi-session trajectories by explicitly modeling how each session contributes, rather than treating all sessions as equally responsible for the final outcome.
engineering_relevance: This matters for real agent systems that use context compaction or subagent forking, because training can now better match inference-time behavior and reduce wasted session usage.
method: Introduces a multi-session RL setting that supports any number of sessions per trajectory.
Uses session-usage signals at the trajectory level to improve advantage estimation.
Estimates each session’s marginal contribution and shapes session-level advantages accordingly, without a critic.
evidence_signal: On BrowseComp with Qwen3.5-4B, Mosaic outperforms trajectory-level broadcasting in both context compaction and subagent forking while using fewer sessions on average.
watch_item: The method relies on estimating marginal session contributions, which may be sensitive to noisy credit assignment and could be harder to stabilize in more complex tasks.
